title: Grade 5 Science — Mon, Jun 16
description: Respiratory System — Day 1 of 5: Why we breathe — breathing vs cellular respiration
subject: science

questions.question: Respiration is:
options: The process of taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide to produce energy
The process of digesting food only
questions.explanation: Respiration is the process of taking in oxygen (O₂) and releasing carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water. Cells use oxygen to release energy from food.

questions.question: Breathing (ventilation) and respiration are:
options: Different: breathing is moving air in and out; respiration is the chemical process releasing energy in cells
questions.explanation: Breathing = physical process of moving air (inhalation/exhalation). Respiration = chemical process in cells using oxygen to release energy from glucose.

questions.question: We breathe because our body cells need:
options: Oxygen to break down glucose and release energy
questions.explanation: Cells need oxygen to perform cellular respiration — they break down glucose (from food) using oxygen to produce energy (ATP), CO₂, and water.

questions.question: The gas we BREATHE IN (inhale) and need is:
questions.explanation: We inhale oxygen (O₂). Air is ~21% oxygen, ~78% nitrogen, ~0.04% CO₂.

questions.question: The gas we BREATHE OUT (exhale) in large amounts is:
questions.explanation: We exhale more CO₂ and water vapour than we inhale. Exhaled air: ~16% O₂, ~4% CO₂ (100x more than inhaled), more water vapour.

questions.question: The simple equation for respiration is:
questions.explanation: Glucose + Oxygen → Carbon dioxide + Water + Energy. Cells use this to power all activities.

questions.question: How many times per minute does an average adult breathe at rest?
questions.explanation: An adult breathes 12–20 times per minute at rest. During exercise, this increases to 40–60 times per minute.

questions.question: Why does breathing rate increase during exercise?
options: Muscles need more oxygen for extra energy; more CO₂ is produced
questions.explanation: During exercise, muscles work harder, need more oxygen, and produce more CO₂. The breathing rate increases to supply more O₂ and remove excess CO₂.

questions.question: The respiratory system includes:
questions.explanation: The respiratory system organs are: nose, nasal passages, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli (in lungs), diaphragm.

questions.question: Air enters the body through:
questions.explanation: Air normally enters through the nose. Breathing through the nose is preferred — nose hairs filter dust; nasal passages warm and moisten the air.

questions.question: Why is it better to breathe through the nose than the mouth?
options: Nose hairs and mucus filter dust and bacteria; nasal passage warms and moistens air
questions.explanation: The nose filters (nose hairs + mucus trap particles), warms (blood vessels warm cold air), and moistens (mucus adds moisture) incoming air before it reaches the lungs.

questions.question: Fish breathe underwater using:
options: Gills — which extract dissolved oxygen from water
questions.explanation: Fish have gills that extract oxygen dissolved in water. Gills pass water over thin membranes with blood vessels — oxygen diffuses in, CO₂ diffuses out.

questions.question: What happens if you hold your breath for too long?
options: CO₂ builds up in the blood, signalling the brain to force breathing
questions.explanation: Rising CO₂ levels in the blood are detected by the brain. The urge to breathe is mainly triggered by HIGH CO₂ (not low oxygen). The brain forces breathing.

questions.question: The respiratory system is linked to the _____ system, which carries oxygen from the lungs to body cells.
questions.explanation: The circulatory system (heart + blood vessels) picks up oxygen from the lungs and carries it to all body cells. These two systems work together closely.

questions.question: Aerobic respiration requires ___; anaerobic respiration does NOT:
questions.explanation: Aerobic = with oxygen (aerobic respiration is what most cells do). Anaerobic = without oxygen (occurs during intense exercise when O₂ supply is insufficient — produces lactic acid).
